Performers
Thérèse Dussaut (piano) Documented[1]
Work version
Original solo-piano work of 1899 Documented

The source credits a pianist and identifies the Pavane as track 5; no performing edition is named.

[1] [3]
Recorded
1976 Inferred, not documented

The Commons footnote reports a WorldCat record with June 1976 for LP side 1 and March 1975 for side 2, and infers that the Pavane belongs to side 1. The catalogue was not independently retrievable, so 1976 remains an inference; the Commons Date field of 1 March 2011 is not a session date.

[1]
Place
Seattle Documented

The source Readme places the first five tracks, including the Pavane, in Seattle. No hall or studio is identified.

[1] [3]
Label
Unknown Unknown

The original release label is not identified.

[1]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

Commons names the LP Ravel: Masterworks and a New Discovery, but does not supply a catalogue number. The cited WorldCat record (OCLC 65925250) was not independently retrievable.

[1]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

No matrix, take or disc-side identifiers are supplied; the digital file format does not establish the original carrier.

[1]
Transfer
Glenn White — original recording engineer Documented

The Readme says the Seattle tracks were recorded by Glenn White. It does not identify the later LP-to-file transfer engineer.

[1] [3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is documented. Upload and transcode dates are not session or transfer dates.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

No source-transfer or restoration processing is disclosed. The access-file encoding is recorded separately.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain in jurisdictions applying an unextended life-plus-70-year term Inferred, not documented

Maurice Ravel died in 1937. This assessment concerns the original composition, not a later edition, arrangement or this recording; it is not a worldwide rights clearance.

[1]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — recording licence/release: CC BY-SA 2.0 (EFF Open Audio License). Documented

Commons explicitly applies cc-by-sa-2.0 and describes the EFF Open Audio License grant for Thérèse Dussaut’s recording. Its attributed 1976 date is later than the historic-recording cutoffs; rule 1, not an age-based rule, is used.
